questions.q: Three weeks after starting an SSRI for what was diagnosed as major depression, a 22-year-old is sleeping 3 hours a night, speaking rapidly, and has spent his tuition money. What does the module direct?
ch: Emergence of mania or hypomania — reassess for bipolar disorder and stop the offending agent
This is a discontinuation syndrome; restart the SSRI at the original dose and taper slowly
This is akathisia from the SSRI; add a beta-blocker and continue at the current dose
This is the expected paradoxical energy surge; continue the SSRI and reassess in two weeks
This is serotonin syndrome; add cyproheptadine and continue the SSRI at a lower dose

questions.q: A patient who frequently misses doses asks which antidepressant is least likely to cause symptoms if a dose is skipped. Which answer matches the module's pearls?
ch: Venlafaxine, because it has both serotonergic and noradrenergic activity

Phenelzine, because monoamine oxidase inhibition is irreversible
Fluoxetine, because its long half-life makes it effectively self-tapering
Paroxetine, because it is highly protein-bound in plasma

Atypical depression — consider an MAOI such as phenelzine
Psychotic depression — consider antipsychotic augmentation or ECT
